-- BA PUTS STRIKE COST AT 125M STG

British Airways has announced that last months three day strike would cost the company 125m stg on top of reduced profits of 77m stg for the last three months because of the strength of the pound, both figures being much higher than analysts forecasts and caused shares to sink 30p to 610p per share yesterday making them the worst performer in the FTSE 100 yesterday.
-- HAMPEL TO SUGGEST APPOINTMENT OF LEAD NON-EXECUTIVE

The draft report from the Hampel committee, published this afternoon, will recommend that one non-executive of each public company should be nominated as a senior independent director to elevate good corporate governance and allow shareholders to use the non-executive directors to express their concerns over executive directors' performance following complaints from institutional shareholders.
-- BOEING COMPLETES MCDONNELL DOUGLAS TAKEOVER

US aircraft manufacturer Boeing yesterday completed its takeover of McDonnel Douglas, making it the world's biggest aerospace and defence company, and indicated its intention not to be impeded by the promises to the European Union to keep its new civil aircraft operations sperate from its defence contracts as chairman Philip Condit announced the necessity to only separate accounts for the businesses.
-- CITY FIRMS WARNED TO TEST FOR SHARES CRASH

Fund management regulator Imro has announced dissatisfaction with city of London firms' ability to cope with a sudden increased demand if a stock market crash occurred, even though many firms had expanded telephone networks and flexible staffing policies, because the continency systems had not been tested to establish their capacity to cope with the flood of small private investors.
-- FRANCE TELECOM FINED FFR30M

Following a complaint by BT, formerly British Telecommunications, the French competition authorities have fined France Telecom FFr30m for abusing its dominant position to win a contract in 1993 with the French insurance group Axa leaving BT open follow up claims for additional damages and interest from the French communications company.
-- TWO PUB CHAINS CALL TIME ON SALE OF ALCOPOPS

Two large pub chains, JD Wetherspoon and Whitbread, have announced a ban on the sale of alcopops from some of their pubs in the wake of the recent government plans to stop under-age drinking and the controversial sale of the alcopops drinks. Wetherspoon has stopped the sale of the drinks in all of its 194 pubs, while Whitbread has removed the drinks from the shelves of 400 of its 1,700 pubs.
-- BUSINESSES SEE IT AS VITAL FOR COMPETITIVENESS

As part of the Department of Trade and Industry's information society initiative programme for business, Spectrum Strategy Consultants have published a research report that identifies that 81 per cent of UK businesses recognise the importance of information and communication technologies for competitiveness, although many small companies could still take further advantages from IT technology.
-- MUSIC GROUP ACQUIRED BY DUTCH RIVAL

Compact disc and audio cassette manufacturer Mayking has been purchased by its Dutch rivals DOCdata for 11m stg after the accountancy group Robson Rhodes were appointed as administrators of the firm after it ran into financial difficulties earlier in the year with over-capacity in the compact disc and audio cassette markets.
-- HSBC UP 13 PER CENT IN FIRST HALF

The worlds biggest bank group, which owns the Hong Kong Bank group and Midland in the UK, HSBC, has announced interim pre-tax profits up 13 per cent to 2.62bn stg surprising investors by increasing its share dividend from 15p to 20p and beating a 26 per cent increase in payouts by the leading UK retail bank, Lloyds TSB. Group chairman Sir Willie Purves warned that the dividend increase would not be maintained all year.
-- NOKIA DOUBLES PROFITS ON STRONG MOBILE PHONE SALES

The worlds second largest supplier of mobile phones, Finnish group Nokia, more than doubled its second quarter profits from FM728m (80.4m stg) last year to FM1.9bn due to 49 per cent increase in mobile phone sales forecasting a boosted half year profits figure from FM1.1bn to FM3.3bn. Nokia's common A shares rose FM9.60 to FM482.10 compared to a marginal share price slip by Swedish rivals Motorola. For a full range of news monitoring services, phone BMC "44-171-377-1742
